specName: Attach a hook from a list, not from memory

capture-runtime: Recording state MUST NOT be able to break the run it observes
The context file is append-only, crash-safe, and tolerant of fields it does not own
Lifecycle status moves forward only, and the terminal state has exactly one writer
Timing is stamped by a script, never hand-authored
Per-task progress is finish-only, contention-free, and folded idempotently
Derived artifacts have exactly one writer
An unresolvable pointer is named, not passed over
The spec a write lands on is resolved by a fixed precedence, and a conflict refuses rather than guesses
Additive capture composes; lifecycle modes are exclusive
Folding a feature spec's requirement deltas into a living spec is idempotent for every verb combination
A probe that cannot determine an answer MUST report "unknown", never the negative
A report MUST NOT claim success for work it did not do
Living-spec path resolution stops at a nested project boundary
Each product ships every module its own entry points reach
The configuration is the source of truth and the command bodies are built from it
A build is all-or-nothing
A built body reaches the assistant only once it is carried out to the agent's own copy
A hook is rendered at the node boundary it names
A build states what each run must produce, derived from the order it assembled
The pipeline's decision points are data, not prose in three places
A template is customized by section, and the stock copy is never edited
Writing one key back into the configuration preserves everything else byte for byte
A configuration too broken to read is repairable from the panel that reads it
The pipeline's structure is emitted here and drawn elsewhere
A bypassed configuration is resolved and drawn, and never allowed to fail the board
A step a project declared is a real step; only a typo is refused
The write lock is released once, after the publish, on whichever path ran
The fold routes each capability's requirements to its own spec
The drift detector offers an opt-in working-tree mode
Recording which living specs cover a change MUST be deterministic, not AI-judged
Completion accounts for every loaded capability — fold it, or record a reasoned skip
An unmatched MODIFIED requirement is promoted to ADDED, not dropped
Status resolution dispatches commands from the family the spec has been running
Every handled call records itself, including the ones that fail
A call count may shrink only when the record it produces stays identical
A capability relocation is transactional — a partial failure rolls back every applied move
A reader of a captured list MUST accept every form its writer stores
A configuration the reader cannot fully read is rejected whole, never applied in part
The health check MUST consult the unrecorded-calls marker before concluding a spec has no trace evidence
The health check MUST report an implement step that closed having executed nothing
A living-spec load is sliced by requirement, and a spec with no markers is read whole
Which requirements a run read is recorded beside which capabilities it loaded

FR-001.title: Attaching offers a list of what this project has, for the chosen kind

FR-002.title: The second selector reacts to the kind selector

FR-003.title: Changing the kind clears a choice made for the previous kind

FR-004.title: Each entry carries a plain-language description where the source has one

FR-005.title: Choosing an entry attaches the hook with that entry exact identifier

FR-006.title: Typing an identifier by hand remains possible for every kind that has one

FR-007.title: The commands come from the project registries, never a compiled-in list

FR-008.title: A command registered for several steps is offered once

FR-009.title: An unreadable or absent registry leaves the form working

FR-010.title: A kind with nothing to offer says so rather than showing an empty control

FR-011.title: The instruction kind shows no second selector, because its value is prose

FR-012.title: An entry says where it usually attaches, and omits that rather than guessing

FR-013.title: Editing in place, moving to another boundary and the note field keep working

context: area: webview/src/pipeline-builder (AttachForm, hookKinds, the Menu component)
constraint: the panel derives nothing a second time; the catalog travels in the graph message
constraint: reading a registry must never fail the panel
intent: Make attaching work to the pipeline a choice from what this project has, rather than a command name you have to already know.
expectations: Drawing the node dependency graph (the #594 half of the merged issue)
Offering extensions that are not installed
Moving or restricting where a hook may attach

decisions.decision: The catalog is built where every other choice is built and travels in the same message
decisions.why: The panel derives structure once and draws it elsewhere; a second fetch is a second source that can disagree with the board beside it
decisions.rejected: A request-on-open message, and a list compiled into the panel that would lie about what is installed

decisions.decision: An offered entry carries a description and a usual placement, not just a name
decisions.why: A list of bare command names asks the same knowledge the free-text box asked, one click earlier; both registries already carry the description

decisions.decision: Render the picker with the panel own menu rather than the existing type-ahead
decisions.why: A datalist only reveals itself once you type something that matches, so a person who does not know the name never sees it, and it has nowhere to put a description
decisions.rejected: Keeping the datalist, and opening a separate dialog

decisions.decision: Usual placement is informational and never restricts where a hook may attach
decisions.why: A project may legitimately attach a hook anywhere, and the pipeline itself does not enforce the convention
decisions.rejected: Filtering the list by the anchor being edited, which hides valid choices

decisions.decision: The same command registered at several steps is offered once
decisions.why: A stock install registers the automatic commit at nine lifecycle steps; nine rows would say nothing true
decisions.rejected: Grouping by step, which turns one choice into two

plan.summary: Plan for a per-project command catalog carried in the graph message, offered through the panel own menu with descriptions, with free text still beside it.
plan.key_finding: The form already cascades and already clears on a kind change — what is missing is that the command kind offers nothing and the entries carry no description.

tasks.summary: 17 tasks in 5 phases and 4 waves: the per-project catalog first, then the picker, then the placement on the row, then the surfaces and the fold.

approach: Add a per-project catalog of installed hook commands to the data the panel already receives, widen offered entries from bare names to entries carrying a description and a usual placement, and show them through the panel's own menu rather than a type-ahead. Typing by hand stays beside the list.

T001.did: Catalog cases: both registries, de-duplication, placement from the lifecycle key, a nameless entry skipped, an unreadable registry, and a command in several places naming none

T002.did: Read every hook command the project registries carry, de-duplicated on the name, with its description, its extension and a placement only where there is exactly one

T003.did: Declared the offered-entry shape and added the command catalog to the choices the panel receives

T004.did: Put the catalog in choices beside skills and nodes, built where every other choice is built

T005.did: Form cases: the list per kind, the descriptions on each row, no choice carried across a kind change, the exact identifier attached, typing still accepted, an empty list said in words, and no picker for an instruction

T006.did: Every kind reads its offerings the same way, so a command is a choice rather than a name you had to know

T007.did: Show the entries through the panel's own menu with the description under each row, and keep the free-text field beside it

T008.did: Say the list is empty rather than showing an empty control, and show no picker for an instruction

T009.did: Registry cases: an extension's hooks with its own words, an absent extension offering nothing, and Companion's own four always present

T010.did: Placement cases: a lifecycle key read as words, and a command registered in several places naming none of them

T011.did: Render the placement and the registering extension on the row, omitting either when absent

T012.did: A story showing the picker on a project with the git extension installed

T013.did: Documented attaching from the list, including why a command in several places names none

T014.did: User-facing release note for choosing a hook instead of spelling it

T015.did: Release note for the catalog the spec-kit side now emits

T016.did: Delta routing the emitted catalog to capture-runtime

T017.did: Validated against the Success Criteria: 2821 Jest, 1308 Python, both compiles, shape parity, command emissions, the shape check, and the catalog verified against this repository's real registry

verified.result: 2821 tests pass, including 8 new AttachForm cases covering the cascade, the clearing and the free-text fallback

verified.what: both compiles, shape parity, command emissions, Storybook build
the catalog against this repository real registry
verified.result: the seven commands the issue names, the automatic commit once with no placement because it is registered at nine steps

concerns.note: Task finishes were journaled in batches rather than one per task. The summaries and their order are trustworthy; the per-task timestamps are not, and history is append-only so this cannot be repaired for this run.

The datalist type-ahead was replaced by the panel menu. A person who knew the old behaviour will find filtering-by-typing no longer narrows a list, though typing a full name still works and the list is now browsable, which is the point of the change.
